correctness.rationale: A feasible nonempty pattern with maximum letter count h shares a constant-letter subsequence of length h with every host of the specified content and has length at most T=min(k, sum_i min(c_i,h)). Conversely one can realize every admissible h with total T and maximum count h by reserving one coordinate of capacity h, then filling the remaining capacities. Placing those counts in reverse block order from the host forces every common subsequence to use one letter and attains T−h. The empty host and pattern give zero. Globally the deficit of a feasible length-m pattern is at most m−ceil(m/q), a nondecreasing function of m. Pure-letter patterns detect the capped count of every letter at any nonnegative budget. Opposite block orders with balanced counts and total length k attain the bound k−ceil(k/q); the reverse host distinguishes itself from the forward host at every lower budget without changing the capped counts. This also covers q=1 and k=1, when no lower nonnegative budget exists, and q>k, when the witness uses k distinct letters.
residual_risks: The finite checks corroborate the algebraic proof; they do not establish the all-parameter result by themselves.

The supported distinct claims are the exact worst-order envelope at every content and the matching necessity at the alphabet-dependent collapse threshold. Inspected more precise subthreshold counts apply to one binary parameter triple, not the general sharp statement.

checked_sources: Frozen RESULT.md, exact content envelope and sharp equivalence-index transition; arXiv:2506.03814v1 §4 and arXiv:2610.17910v1 Proposition 10/Corollary 11
value.rationale: The exact envelope determines how much order can cost at a prescribed content, including highly unbalanced contents where the worst-case alphabet bound is far from attained. The sharp collapse theorem answers exactly when all order information disappears from this established equivalence model, rather than giving another nonoptimal sufficient budget. The two statements are useful despite not classifying the subthreshold quotient.
residual_risks: The content envelope is a maximum over orderings, not the deficit of each particular host, and the result does not enumerate all subthreshold classes.
